title: PostgreSQL Installation & Configuration
description: Install PostgreSQL on Linux, macOS, and Docker, configure pg_hba.conf, and secure client authentication with SCRAM-SHA-256.

data.text: Getting started with PostgreSQL can be done via native package managers (APT, YUM, Homebrew) or through containerization with Docker. In modern engineering, Docker is preferred for local development to ensure consistent engine versions.

data.title: docker-compose.yml for Local Development
data.content: Spins up PostgreSQL 16 with a persistent volume and healthcheck.
data.code:
version: '3.8'
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    container_name: dev-postgres
    restart: always
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app_user
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secure_dev_password
      POSTGRES_DB: app_development
    ports:
      - '5432:5432'
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U app_user -d app_development']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

volumes:
  pgdata:

data.text: Host-Based Authentication is controlled by the `pg_hba.conf` configuration file. It evaluates connection requests in top-down order. The modern industry standard is **scram-sha-256**, which provides mutual password authentication and protects against replay attacks.

data.title: pg_hba.conf Secure Authentication Rules
data.content: Configuring local socket and IPv4/IPv6 client permissions.
data.code:
# TYPE  DATABASE        USER            ADDRESS                 METHOD
# Local Unix domain socket connections
local   all             all                                     peer
# IPv4 local connections:
host    all             all             127.0.0.1/32            scram-sha-256
# IPv6 local connections:
host    all             all             ::1/128                 scram-sha-256
# Internal Docker / VPC subnet:
host    all             all             10.0.0.0/16             scram-sha-256

items.text: Configure `listen_addresses = '*'` only if behind a secure private VPC
items.hint: Never expose port 5432 to public internet

items.text: Create dedicated unprivileged users per application
items.hint: Never use the postgres superuser in web applications

items.text: Verify automated backups with pg_dump or pgBackRest

data.text: Containers are excellent for a consistent development environment, but production installs usually come from the distribution packages. Knowing both is expected for a backend or DBA role.

data.title: Installing PostgreSQL 16 Natively
data.content: Debian/Ubuntu uses the PostgreSQL APT repository, macOS uses Homebrew.
data.code:
# --- Debian / Ubuntu ---
sudo apt install -y postgresql-common
sudo /usr/share/postgresql-common/pgdg/apt.postgresql.org.sh
sudo apt install -y postgresql-16
sudo systemctl enable --now postgresql

# --- macOS (Homebrew) ---
brew install postgresql@16
brew services start postgresql@16

# --- Verify the cluster is listening ---
pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432        # => localhost:5432 - accepting connections
psql -h localhost -U postgres -c "SELECT version();"

rows: The data directory: heap files, `pg_wal`, `pg_xact`. This is what you back up.
Server logs; the first place to look when startup fails.

data.text: The Settings You Actually Change First

data.title: A Minimal, Sensible postgresql.conf Baseline
data.content: These four settings matter more than the other three hundred.
data.code:
# Identify the server for logs and monitoring
listen_addresses = 'localhost'        # '*' only behind a private network
port = 5432

# Correct memory and disk assumptions
shared_buffers = 4GB                  # start at ~25% of RAM
effective_cache_size = 12GB           # tell the planner what the OS cache holds
maintenance_work_mem = 512MB          # used by VACUUM and CREATE INDEX

# Durability / write throughput
wal_level = replica                   # required for streaming replication
max_wal_size = 4GB
synchronous_commit = on               # 'off' risks losing recent commits on crash

# Logging that pays for itself
log_min_duration_statement = 500      # log anything slower than 500 ms
log_checkpoints = on
log_lock_waits = on

data.text: After editing, reload the config without dropping connections: `SELECT pg_reload_conf();` or `sudo systemctl reload postgresql`. Only parameters marked `postmaster` require a full restart.

data.title: Never Set `listen_addresses = '*'` on a Public Host
data.text: An internet-reachable `5432` will be probed for weak passwords within minutes. Bind to localhost or a private subnet, and put TLS plus a firewall in front of anything remote.

items.text: Install from the official PostgreSQL repository, not a stale distro package
items.hint: You want at least PostgreSQL 14 for modern features

items.text: Set `password_encryption = scram-sha-256` and re-set existing passwords
Create one unprivileged role per application, not shared credentials
Restrict `pg_hba.conf` to the networks that need access
Configure and **test a restore** before you need one

items.question: Docker or native install for development?
items.answer: Docker for reproducibility across a team (identical version and extensions); native when you need to test OS-level tuning, extensions compiled against the system libs, or replication between local instances.

items.question: What does `initdb` do?
items.answer: It creates a new data directory and cluster: `initdb -D /var/lib/postgresql/data` initialises catalogs, a default `postgres` database, and the `template1` template. Package installs already call it for you.

items.question: What is the difference between `pg_hba.conf` and `postgresql.conf`?
items.answer: `pg_hba.conf` answers "who may connect and how are they authenticated"; `postgresql.conf` configures server behaviour such as memory, WAL, and logging.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Docker Compose gives teams a reproducible local engine; native packages are the norm in production.
`PGDATA` holds the actual data — that is the directory your backup strategy protects.
`pg_hba.conf` is evaluated top-down and decides authentication; `scram-sha-256` is the modern default.
The highest-impact first settings are `shared_buffers`, `effective_cache_size`, `max_wal_size`, and slow-query logging.
Reload with `pg_reload_conf()`; only `postmaster`-level parameters require a restart.
data.takeaway: Be able to state the four files: `postgresql.conf`, `pg_hba.conf`, `PGDATA`, and the server log.
